merger_name: Coles – supermarket site in Coffs Harbour (NSW)
merger_description:
Coles Group Limited (Coles) is an Australian public company (ASX: COL) that primarily operates:

* supermarkets nationwide through its subsidiary, Coles Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd; and
* retail liquor stores nationwide, trading under the Liquorland, Liquorland Warehouse and Liquorland Cellars brands.

H.A. Bachrach (Nom) Pty Ltd (the Lessor) is a part of an Australian private property development company, the Bachrach Naumburger Group, which manages a portfolio of commercial office and retail properties in Queensland.

Coles has signed a letter of offer in respect of a proposed lease for the development of a Coles supermarket within an existing shopping centre known as Park Beach Plaza, located at 253 Pacific Highway, Coffs Harbour, NSW 2450 (the **Acquisition**). The site was previously occupied by a Ritchies IGA Supermarket which closed at the end of April 2026.

The proposed Coles supermarket is anticipated to open in September 2027.

events.title: Coles - supermarket site in Coffs Harbour (NSW) - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Coles Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of Coles Group
Limited (Coles), proposes to acquire a leasehold interest for the
development of a Coles supermarket within an existing shopping
centre located at 253 Pacific Highway, Coffs Harbour, NSW 2450
(the Target Site) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Coles, is an Australian public company (ASX: COL) that
primarily operates:
• supermarkets nationwide through its subsidiary, Coles
Supermarkets Australia Pty Ltd; and
• retail liquor stores nationwide, trading under the Liquorland,
Liquorland Warehouse and Liquorland Cellars brands.
The lessor, H.A. Bachrach (Nom) Pty Ltd, is a part of an Australian
private property development company, the Bachrach Naumburger
Group, which manages a portfolio of commercial office and retail
properties in Queensland.
The Target Site is within the Park Beach Plaza shopping centre
located at 253 Pacific Highway, Coffs Harbour NSW, which contains
a Woolworths and ALDI.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the parties
determination_table_content.details:
The leasehold interest is an input to Coles’ existing supermarket
retailing operations, which would facilitate Coles establishing the
new supermarket.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, other information provided by the parties and
publicly available sources.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The proposed Coles supermarket would face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers in the surrounding area.
• The aggregation arising from the Acquisition is not sufficient to
meaningfully change competition in the relevant local market.
• The Acquisition does not result in the removal of a competitor.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
